falsifier: a re-score of each Baseline's own artifact reproduces its published must-find and reference coverage
hypothesis: the figures on the Baselines page were computed by the scorer and corpus at each merge, so re-scoring the same archived sweep today reads a different number
intervention: re-scored all three merged Baselines to copies with 'run score --out' and compared the pooled counts against the numbers their own artifacts carry
reconsider_when: the comparison prints a re-scored column, or a Baseline is merged at the current corpus digest
scope: the three merged Baselines under evals/baselines/, stride only, scorer and corpus at this revision. Says nothing about which side is right.
signature: a Baseline figure published in evals/baselines/README.md does not reproduce when its own sweep is re-scored today

falsifier: the critic-yield instrument shows few drafts killed and few must-finds lost for good
hypothesis: the critic destroys enough correct drafts to be a leading cause of the missed must-finds
intervention: read the critic-yield block of the re-scored 2198870 Baseline
reconsider_when: a sweep of a different model, or a critic prompt change
scope: the 2198870 Baseline, stride, 13 cases, one sweep. A single sweep, so a rare destructive pass would not show.
signature: STRIDE must-find coverage sits near half on every merged Baseline

falsifier: a perfect reading of every signed case survives the deterministic path with no loss
hypothesis: the deterministic code between the reading model and the catalog drops facts, so extraction loses them before a lane can read them
intervention: ran the oracle instrument over the signed corpus
reconsider_when: the assertion schema or the resolver changes, or a new case is signed
scope: the 13 signed corpus cases and the 122 required rows their reference facts carry. Says nothing about what a model reads.
signature: STRIDE must-find coverage sits near half on every merged Baseline

falsifier: run score prints a comparability warning naming both digests
hypothesis: nothing in the tooling tells a reader that a re-score crossed a corpus digest, so the crossing is silent
intervention: re-read the whole score output rather than grepping it for the coverage lines
reconsider_when: never for this fact; the lesson is that an audit reads an instrument whole
scope: run score at this revision. The warning exists and names both digests; #1083 added it.
signature: a Baseline figure published in evals/baselines/README.md does not reproduce when its own sweep is re-scored today

falsifier: the matched reference indices move both ways, which a reference correction does and an identifier move does not
hypothesis: the drop is scorer drift, so a fix measured against a published figure carries that much scorer movement
intervention: diffed the matched (case, reference_index) pairs between each Baseline as merged and re-scored
reconsider_when: a Baseline is cut on the current corpus digest, which gives a comparison that needs none of this
scope: the three merged Baselines. 2198870 lost 16 and gained 0; d3f1898 lost 14 and gained 0; both ran on corpus b09805c6726d. d4edd64, on its own digest 09772afde754, lost 14 and gained 5.
signature: a Baseline figure published in evals/baselines/README.md does not reproduce when its own sweep is re-scored today

falsifier: the gateway refuses on dispatch, which it does on reserved output rather than on expected spend
hypothesis: the remaining openrouter balance is enough to pre-flight one STRIDE case, because the case is expected to cost about a third of it
intervention: ran one case, 01-payments-checkout, stride, analysis mode, with --accept-cost unknown on openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-terra
reconsider_when: the openrouter balance is topped up, or the route moves to direct openai, which is priced
scope: openrouter only, at a 0.78 USD account balance, six lane agents dispatched together at 64000 max output tokens each. Says nothing about the direct openai route.
signature: an openrouter sweep is refused on dispatch with 402 in_flight_budget_exhausted

falsifier: a node serves a build other than the one requested, the upstream pin does not hold, or no fingerprint is recorded
hypothesis: the openrouter route carries the analysis machinery end to end once the balance clears the dispatch reservation
intervention: topped the balance to 20.78 USD and re-ran the identical one-case command
reconsider_when: litellm is bumped, or the openrouter row's served_trust changes
scope: one case, eight strong-tier nodes. Requested and served both openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-terra, served_upstream OpenAI, one fingerprint 26d18056 across all eight. Says nothing about whether the case completes.
signature: an openrouter sweep is refused on dispatch with 402 in_flight_budget_exhausted

falsifier: the run completes case 01 and writes a report
hypothesis: a Baseline can be cut on this tree today, because the machinery and the route both work
intervention: ran case 01, stride, analysis mode, on openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-terra
reconsider_when: a repeat of case 01 says whether the gate fires deterministically
scope: one observation, one model, one case. A single stochastic failure is suggestive and not proof that the gate fires every time.
signature: the critic rules a claim confirmed while dismissing an unknown its own grounds do not cite, and the Tier 1 gate stops the sweep

falsifier: a repeat of the identical command completes the case and writes a report
hypothesis: the Tier 1 critic gate fires on every run of case 01, so the case cannot pass on this tree
intervention: re-ran the identical one-case command a second time
reconsider_when: more runs of case 01 give the gate a rate rather than a yes or no
scope: two runs of one case on one model: one aborted at the gate, one completed with must-find 7 of 11 and reference coverage 0.545. One failure in two says the gate is not deterministic and says almost nothing about its rate.
signature: the critic rules a claim confirmed while dismissing an unknown its own grounds do not cite, and the Tier 1 gate stops the sweep

falsifier: the artifact carries the critic's emitted ruling and the draft it judged
hypothesis: the aborted run archived enough to diagnose the critic offline, so the next step costs nothing
intervention: read every block of the aborted run's artifact and its reports directory
reconsider_when: a run archives what a failing node emitted
scope: analysis mode, Tier 1 structural gating. The artifact carries the error string in structural_failures and mode_output, an empty reports directory, and no emitted ruling anywhere.
signature: a Tier 1 critic failure archives its message and not the output that caused it

falsifier: a case aborts at a Tier 1 gate, which ends the sweep and leaves a partial artifact no Baseline may hold
hypothesis: a full STRIDE sweep on the current tree completes and can be sealed, ending the arithmetic that every re-score needed
intervention: ran the whole 13-case corpus, stride, analysis mode, on openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-terra and submitted it
reconsider_when: the corpus digest or the prompts move again
scope: one sweep of 13 cases at commit 6bff717 and corpus d5f345c2. Pooled must-find 73 of 129 and reference 105 of 244. One sweep, so it carries no spread of its own.
signature: no merged Baseline runs on the corpus digest that stands, so every published figure is a record of an older yardstick

falsifier: a sweep on the tree that stands charges the critic a share of must-find losses comparable to the generation classes
hypothesis: the critic is not a leading cause of missed must-finds, which the 2198870 Baseline supported
intervention: read the losses block of the 6bff717 Baseline
reconsider_when: a second sweep of this configuration gives the critic charge a spread
scope: the 6bff717 Baseline, one sweep. The critic is charged 10 losses and 7 must-finds here against 1 loss and 0 must-finds on 2198870; the two sweeps ran on different corpora and different prompts, so this is not a measured regression.
signature: STRIDE must-find coverage sits near half on every merged Baseline

falsifier: a candidate priced on the frontier loses must-finds, or merges pairs the corpus records as two findings
hypothesis: adding the disagreeing verb pairs to EQUIVALENT recovers the must-finds the verb class loses, which is one of the two options #426 leaves open
intervention: priced six candidate pairs on the frontier against the 6bff717 Baseline with run.py price-verbs, individually and together
reconsider_when: the corpus re-blesses a verb, which changes which pairs disagree at all
scope: six pairs drawn from the equal-place verb rows of the 6bff717 Baseline. Every pair priced alone loses must-finds: replay=guess-credential -2, alter-in-transit=inject -1, alter-in-transit=plant -2, abuse-grant=escalate -2, impersonate=use-credential -1, disable=flood -2. All six together read +5, bought with 13 merges against the shipped rule's 3, nine of which the corpus records as two findings.
signature: the lane cites the reference's place and writes another action, at an equal place
